hints: Use the parallel-side vector relation to reconstruct the missing vertex.
walkthrough:
Express the position vector of $D$ using $\overrightarrow{DC} = \overrightarrow{OC} - \overrightarrow{OD}$:
$$\overrightarrow{OD} = \overrightarrow{OC} - \overrightarrow{DC} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 2 \\ -3 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 6 \\ 3 \\ -6 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 - 6 \\ 2 - 3 \\ -3 - (-6) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -4 \\ -1 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$$

hints: A vector line is a known point plus a scalar multiple of a direction vector.
Use $\overrightarrow{OA}$ as the fixed point and $\overrightarrow{AB}=\overrightarrow{OB}-\overrightarrow{OA}$ as the direction.
Write the equation with a real parameter and all three components.
walkthrough:
Write the vector equation of the line passing through point $A$ with direction vector $\overrightarrow{AB}$:
$$\mathbf{r} = \overrightarrow{OA} + \lambda\overrightarrow{AB}$$

hints: Find the perpendicular separation of the parallel sides by projecting a connecting vector perpendicular to their common direction.
Let a general point $P$ on $AB$ have parameter $\lambda$ and impose $\overrightarrow{CP}\cdot(2,1,-2)=0$.
Solve for $\lambda$ and calculate the length of the resulting perpendicular vector.
Use the parallel side lengths $|AB|$ and $|DC|=3|AB|$ in the trapezium area formula.
walkthrough:
Find the perpendicular distance from point $C(2, 2, -3)$ to the line through $A$ and $B$:
Let $P$ be a point on line $AB$ with position vector $\overrightarrow{OP} = \begin{pmatrix} -1 + 2\lambda \\ 2 + \lambda \\ 3 - 2\lambda \end{pmatrix}$.

Calculate the perpendicular distance $h$ between the parallel sides:
$$h = |\overrightarrow{CP}| = \sqrt{1^2 + 2^2 + 2^2} = \sqrt{1 + 4 + 4} = \sqrt{9} = 3$$

Calculate the lengths of the two parallel sides $AB$ and $DC$:
$$AB = |\overrightarrow{AB}| = \sqrt{2^2 + 1^2 + (-2)^2} = \sqrt{4 + 1 + 4} = \sqrt{9} = 3$$
$$DC = 3AB = 3(3) = 9$$

Calculate the area of the trapezium:
$$\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2}(AB + DC) \times h = \dfrac{1}{2}(3 + 9) \times 3 = \dfrac{1}{2}(12) \times 3 = 18$$
